items.statement: Dye1 low-energy absorption has electronic transition support
items.expected: Actual transition-orbital, density or physically comparable state-character evidence assigns the low-energy dye1 absorption to the conjugated molecular pi system and identifies the participating imine/aromatic/organoboron regions. The intact supplied graph and declared solvent representation determine eligibility; neither a particular gas geometry nor private SI-table numbering is required. A matched wavelength or orbital-gap value without electronic assignment fails.

items.statement: Dye2 low-energy absorption has electronic transition support
items.expected: Actual transition-orbital, density or physically comparable state-character evidence assigns dye2 low-energy absorption to the correctly methoxy-substituted molecular pi system and resolves the regions involved in redistribution. Intact supplied identity and a declared solution/model state are required. A source gas calculation or knowledge of private SI compound-number conflicts is not required; a peak label alone is insufficient.

items.statement: Intact-dye electronic structure explains the relative long-band order
items.expected: Conclude that the chemically mapped methoxy substitution changes the electronic transition distribution on the intact framework and accounts for the dye2 versus dye1 long-band blue ordering. Link actual state-character evidence with comparative energies and supplied spectra, rather than claiming that every electron donor necessarily red-shifts every band.

For intact dye1, actual corresponding-state calculations in CHCl3 and MeOH establish differential ground/excited electronic stabilization consistent with the observed higher absorption energy in MeOH. Explain the sign using computed electronic redistribution or an equivalent solvation analysis. The supplied experimental blue direction alone earns no credit. State the model contribution and any unresolved specific-solvation effects; a two-solvent comparison does not isolate viscosity. No exact shift magnitude is imposed.

For intact dye2, actual corresponding-state calculations in CHCl3 and MeOH establish differential ground/excited electronic stabilization consistent with the observed higher absorption energy in MeOH. Explain the sign using computed electronic redistribution or an equivalent solvation analysis. The supplied experimental blue direction alone earns no credit. State the model contribution and any unresolved specific-solvation effects; a two-solvent comparison does not isolate viscosity. No exact shift magnitude is imposed.

items.statement: Relative electronic response is distinct from absolute band reconstruction
items.expected: Quantitatively compare the actual molecular-model absorption predictions with the supplied solution bands using a defensible state/band correspondence, and conclude separately which relative trends and absolute positions that model supports. Explicit residuals and the vertical-transition versus measured-band distinction must support the adequacy assessment; a fitted offset, favorable root switching or bare limitations paragraph fails. A supported improved solution model may establish absolute agreement; a source-gas baseline or its particular50–60nm residual is not mandatory for AR. The known source baseline discrepancy remains evaluator provenance, not an extra AR computation.
